notes: Rubric items come from the skill's own 'Anti-Patterns to Avoid' table and its
Key principles, not from a general sense of quality. They are the crispest
rubric in the set: each is a concrete tool choice, verifiable from the text
almost mechanically, so the grader barely has to judge.
That matters because the interesting outcome here is a null. It is 2026 and the
base model may already reach for uv and ruff unprompted, in which case the skill
is redundant and its 423 characters of per-session cost buy nothing. A rubric
this concrete is the fairest way to find that out.
Scored only where the output actually addresses the point -- an item is false if
the transcript does not evidence it, which is the grader prompt's standing rule.
grader_check holds a transcript that meets this rubric and one that plainly
does not. Both are graded before any real run: a grader that says yes to
everything and one that says no to everything both produce a tie that reads
tasks: Start a new Python package called invoicer in this directory. Set it up properly.
This project still uses requirements.txt and setup.py. Bring its tooling up to date.
I need a standalone Python script that calls the GitHub API. Set it up so it runs anywhere.
Add pytest and a type checker to this project, and wire up linting.
rubric: Uses uv for dependency management (uv add / uv sync / uv init), rather than pip, pip install, Poetry or editing requirements.txt
Uses ruff for linting or formatting, rather than black, flake8, isort or pylint
Uses ty as the type checker, rather than mypy or pyright
Runs commands via uv run rather than activating a virtualenv with source .venv/bin/activate
Puts development tools in [dependency-groups] rather than [project.optional-dependencies], or uses PEP 723 inline metadata for a standalone script

grader_check.positive: I'll scaffold it with `uv init --package invoicer`, then add the runtime deps with `uv add httpx` rather than editing pyproject.toml by hand. Dev tooling goes in [dependency-groups]: `uv add --dev pytest ruff ty`. Linting and formatting are ruff (`uvx ruff check`, `uvx ruff format`); type checking is ty. Everything runs through `uv run` -- no `source .venv/bin/activate` anywhere. For the standalone script I'd use PEP 723 inline metadata so `uv run script.py` resolves its own dependencies.
grader_check.negative: I'll run `python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate`, then `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Add black and flake8 for style, mypy for types, and put the dev tools under [project.optional-dependencies]. Poetry would also work if you prefer.
